neighbours.label: Action verb of a historical ruler or army in chronicle narrative (William marched, legions advanced on, armies crossed into), vs the same verbs with modern everyday subjects
fire: In 1415 King Henry marched north from Harfleur toward Calais.
After the treaty failed, Charlemagne invaded Saxony with a large host.
That autumn the Roman legions advanced on the Gallic hill fort.
In 1644 the Manchu armies swept south and seized Beijing.
The young king rode out on a royal progress through Kent and Sussex.
In 1240 the Mongol horde attacked Kiev and burned the city.
Saladin then marched on Jerusalem and besieged it in 1187.
Alexander crossed the Hellespont with his army in the spring of 334 BC.
quiet: On Monday the school band marched north from the gym to the field.
After the meeting failed, the manager invited Sam to lunch.
That autumn the hikers advanced slowly up the muddy hill path.
Last year the delivery vans swept the streets for parcels.
The young student rode out on her bike through the park.
Last night the neighbour's dog attacked a cushion and chewed it.
Our team then marched into the office to present the plan.
The tourists crossed the bridge with their guide in the spring.

predictions: Chronicle verbs 0.4-1.3; modern subjects with marched/progress/advanced stay under 0.05.
notes: Card: ' marched' after Louis and Cao Cao (-20.38, -19.25), royal ' progress', ' armies', 'advanced on', поход.
